data.name: Rule_social_contributions
data.value: The final contributions of a self-employed person in main occupation, owed on the year's net taxable professional income: one rate up to a first ceiling, a lower rate up to a second ceiling, nothing above it, and never less than the contribution on the minimum income. The social insurance fund bills them in four equal quarters, each rounded to the cent. The contributions lower the very income they are computed on, so the two are solved together.

data.name: Rule_flat_rate_costs
data.value: A director who does not prove real professional costs deducts flat-rate costs: a percentage of the pay left after the social contributions, up to a yearly maximum. They lower the taxable income and are never paid out.

data.name: Rule_taxable_income
data.value: Gross pay less your own social contributions and the flat-rate costs. The net professional income is never below zero.

data.name: Rule_income_tax
data.value: The progressive scale applied to the taxable income, less the reduction for the tax-free amount, gives the State tax. The federal government keeps that tax less the autonomy factor, and Wallonia adds its regional tax on the federal share. Each of the two is rounded to the cent, and the income tax is their sum.

data.name: Rule_municipal_surcharge
data.value: Your municipality's rate applied to the income tax, that is the federal share plus the Walloon tax.

data.name: Rule_low_earned_income_credit
data.value: A federal tax credit on a modest taxable income from your own work, which a self-employed director's pay is. It rises from nothing to its full amount, stays there, then falls back to nothing at the ceiling. It comes off after the municipal surcharge, which it leaves as it is, and what your tax does not absorb is refunded. Your dividend, taxed at source and not declared, does not count; a director under an employment contract or in a side activity does not get it.

data.name: Rule_corporate_tax
data.value: The company's taxable income is its profit after your director pay, with what it cannot deduct of the vouchers added back; no other disallowed expenses and no losses carried forward. A small company pays the reduced rate on a first slice and the standard rate on the rest. From its fifth tax period, it keeps the reduced rate only if a director's pay reaches the minimum, or if its taxable income does not exceed that pay; otherwise the standard rate applies to all of it.

data.name: Rule_dividend_withholding
data.value: The company withholds tax on the dividend it pays you, at the rate you declare: the standard rate, or a reduced rate for VVPRbis shares, which applies from the second accounting year after the one of the capital contribution. The withholding is the final tax on the dividend: no income tax, no municipal surcharge and no social contributions come on top.

data.name: Rule_dividend_exemption_refund
data.value: The first slice of ordinary dividends a person receives each year is exempt from personal tax. The company still withholds on it, so you declare that withholding in your return and it is credited back, even when you owe no other tax.

data.name: Rule_advance_payment_surcharge
data.value: Corporate tax the company did not pay in advance during the year is increased: the tax times a multiple of the reference rate, less a credit for each advance payment, a smaller multiple of it the later the deadline it was paid by. A company has no threshold below which nothing is due and no bonus for paying more: what is paid beyond the tax is refunded. A small company owes none on the tax of its first three financial years. The surcharge is not deductible, so it does not lower the taxable income.

data.name: Title_income_tax_advance_payment_surcharge
data.value: Advance-payment surcharge on your tax

data.name: Rule_income_tax_advance_payment_surcharge
data.value: The income tax on your director pay, taken alone without any rent taxed with it, that was neither withheld by the company nor paid in advance by you during the year is increased. The base is the tax at 106%, less what was withheld and the tax credit for low earned income you get. It is surcharged at a multiple of the reference rate, less a credit for each advance payment, a smaller multiple of it the later the deadline it was paid by, and 90% of what is left is due. Nothing is due when that is under the minimum or under its share of the base, nor in the first three years of a first self-employed activity.

data.name: Title_income_tax_advance_payment_bonus
data.value: Bonus on your advance payments

data.name: Rule_income_tax_advance_payment_bonus
data.value: Your advance payments count first towards what avoids the surcharge, the earliest first. What you paid beyond that earns a bonus, a smaller multiple of the reference rate the later the deadline it was paid by, on at most the tax at 106% less what was withheld, the tax credits and the payments that avoid the surcharge. Beyond that, what you paid is refunded.

data.name: Rule_withholding
data.value: What the company withholds each month on your pay, by the administration's key formula: the month's pay less a reduction in place of social deductions, times twelve, less the flat-rate professional costs, is the annual net taxable amount. The basic tax on it by the scale of annex III, with a 7% municipal surcharge built in, less the tax on the tax-free amount of a single person, is the annual tax, never below zero, and a twelfth of it is withheld. Each step is rounded to the cent. Over the year the amounts withheld are set against your final tax on the assessment.

data.name: Title_assessment_balance
data.value: Balance on your assessment

data.name: Rule_assessment_balance
data.value: Your assessment charges the final tax on your year's income, your pay and any rent the company pays you, which is taxed with it: the income tax with the municipal surcharge, less the tax credit for low earned income, plus the advance-payment surcharge and less the bonus. What the company withheld on your pay over the year and what you paid in advance are set against it: what is left is to pay, and what was paid beyond it is refunded.

data.name: Title_meal_vouchers
data.value: Meal vouchers

data.name: Rule_meal_vouchers
data.value: The company's share of an electronic meal voucher is exempt for you, so it is neither taxed as pay nor counted in the income your social contributions are owed on, as long as the exemption's conditions hold. Netto gives each voucher the most the company may pay into it, the only share that earns the higher deduction; your own share, at least the amount set, buys the rest of the voucher and moves nothing.

data.name: Title_eco_vouchers
data.value: Eco vouchers

data.name: Rule_eco_vouchers
data.value: Eco vouchers, for ecological products and services, are exempt for you up to a yearly maximum, each of a face value the agreement sets, at most the amount below. Neither taxed as pay nor counted for your social contributions.

data.name: Title_sport_culture_vouchers
data.value: Sport/culture vouchers

data.name: Rule_sport_culture_vouchers
data.value: Sport/culture vouchers are exempt for you up to a yearly maximum. Neither taxed as pay nor counted for your social contributions.

data.name: Title_disallowed_vouchers
data.value: What the company cannot deduct of the vouchers

data.name: Rule_disallowed_vouchers
data.value: An exempt benefit is not a professional expense for the company, with one exception: of each meal voucher it deducts a fixed amount, raised when its share reaches the most it may pay. The rest of each meal voucher, and the whole of the eco and sport/culture vouchers, is a disallowed expense, added back to its taxable income. Paid out, it still leaves the company's profit.

data.name: Title_office_allowance
data.value: Office allowance

data.name: Rule_office_allowance
data.value: A flat-rate allowance for an office in your home covers every office cost: the room and its rent, utilities, supplies, upkeep. The company pays back a cost that is its own, so it is not pay: neither taxed nor counted in the income your social contributions are owed on, and the company deducts it. The administration accepts at most, each month, the amount ONSS accepts, which changes during the year.

data.name: Title_internet_allowance
data.value: Internet allowance

data.name: Rule_internet_allowance
data.value: A flat-rate allowance for the professional use of your private internet connection, up to a fixed amount a month that is not indexed. The company pays back a cost that is its own: not pay, and the company deducts it.

data.name: Title_computer_allowance
data.value: Computer allowance

data.name: Rule_computer_allowance
data.value: A flat-rate allowance for the professional use of your private computer and its peripherals, up to a fixed amount a month that is not indexed. The company pays back a cost that is its own: not pay, and the company deducts it.

data.name: Title_phone_costs
data.value: Phone costs

data.name: Rule_phone_costs
data.value: The professional share of your own phone bills, reimbursed on invoices: no official text sets a flat amount for a phone. The company pays back a cost that is its own: not pay, and the company deducts it.

data.name: Title_rent
data.value: Rent for your home office

data.name: Rule_rent
data.value: The rent the company pays you for the part of your home it uses as an office, unfurnished, reaches your pocket, and the company deducts all of it like its other costs. Kept at or below the cap, 5/3 of the cadastral income of the part let revalued by the year's coefficient, none of it is director pay; above it, the excess would be taxed as pay, with social contributions and no charges deducted.

data.name: Title_rent_charges
data.value: Flat charges on the rent

data.name: Rule_rent_charges
data.value: A built property let to a company is taxed on its rent less 40% for maintenance and repairs, at most 2/3 of the cadastral income of the part let revalued by the year's coefficient: at the cap, the 40% is that limit exactly. They lower the taxable rent and are never paid out.

data.name: Title_rent_taxable_income
data.value: Taxable rent

data.name: Rule_rent_taxable_income
data.value: The rent, never less than the cadastral income of the part let, indexed by the year's coefficient, plus 40%, less its flat charges. It is income from immovable property, taxed with your pay; not professional income, so no social contributions are owed on it.

data.name: Title_car_costs
data.value: The car's costs

data.name: Rule_car_costs
data.value: What the car costs the company over the year, as it bears them: a cost of the company, like its running costs, which lowers its profit. An electric car ordered or leased before 2027 stays deductible in full; another car at the rate its order or lease date, its engine and its CO2 give, beyond the part equal to your benefit taxed and your contribution, which stays deductible up to the costs.

data.name: Title_car_costs_not_deductible
data.value: Costs the company cannot deduct

data.name: Rule_car_costs_not_deductible
data.value: The part of the car's costs beyond your benefit taxed and your contribution that its deduction rate leaves out. It is added back to the company's taxable income; the part equal to your benefit and contribution stays deductible.

data.name: Title_car_benefit
data.value: Car's benefit in kind before your contribution

data.name: Rule_car_benefit
data.value: 6/7 of the catalogue value times the car's CO2 percentage, at the share of the catalogue value the car's age leaves, each part of the year weighed by its days; never less than the year's minimum. The percentage is 5.5% at the year's reference emission for the car's fuel, a tenth of a point more or less for each gram above or below it, between 4%, which a car that emits no CO2 takes, and 18%.

data.name: Title_car_contribution
data.value: Your contribution

data.name: Rule_car_contribution
data.value: What you pay the company for the car's private use. It comes off the benefit you are taxed on, after the minimum, and leaves your pocket for the company.

data.name: Title_car_benefit_taxed
data.value: Car's benefit in kind after your contribution

data.name: Rule_car_benefit_taxed
data.value: The benefit less your contribution, never below zero. It is director pay never paid in cash: in your social contributions' base, your income tax and the monthly withholding.

data.name: Title_car_add_back
data.value: Added back by the company

data.name: Rule_car_add_back
data.value: A share of the benefit before your contribution joins the company's taxable income: 17%, or 40% when the company pays your private charging.

data.name: Title_rent_income_tax
data.value: Income tax on the rent

data.name: Rule_rent_income_tax
data.value: The taxable rent joins the taxable income of your pay: the progressive scale and the tax-free amount apply to both together. What that adds to the income tax on your pay alone is the rent's.

data.name: Title_rent_municipal_surcharge
data.value: Municipal surcharge on the rent

data.name: Rule_rent_municipal_surcharge
data.value: Your municipality's rate applied to the income tax the rent adds.

data.name: Title_rent_low_earned_income_credit_lost
data.value: Tax credit for low earned income the rent takes away

data.name: Rule_rent_low_earned_income_credit_lost
data.value: The credit follows your pay, but your total net income, the rent included, limits it: none above the ceiling, and from where the full credit ends up to the ceiling, at most what the same falling line gives on that total. What the rent takes away of the credit your pay alone would get is lost.

data.name: Title_rent_child_tax_credit_lost
data.value: Tax credit for children the rent takes away

data.name: Rule_rent_child_tax_credit_lost
data.value: The rent is taxed with your pay, so it uses the tax-free amount your children's supplements raised. What it uses of the part the tax could not absorb, which would have been refunded as the credit for children, is lost.

data.name: Rule_child_tax_credit
data.value: Your children raise the tax-free amount. When your income is too low for the tax on it to absorb all of that, the part due to the children's supplements is refunded as a tax credit, up to a cap per child. It comes off after the municipal surcharge, and what your tax does not absorb is refunded. In a joint return it is your household's.

data.name: Title_rent_income_tax_advance_payments
data.value: Advance-payment surcharge the lost credit adds

data.name: Rule_rent_income_tax_advance_payments
data.value: The advance-payment surcharge is on the tax on your pay taken alone, so the rent's own tax is never surcharged. But its base is that tax at 106% less what was withheld and the credit you actually get: a credit the rent takes away raises it, and with it the surcharge, less any change in the bonus.

data.name: Title_copyright_royalty
data.value: Copyright royalty

data.name: Rule_copyright_royalty
data.value: The royalty the company pays you for the rights on your works, deducted in full like its other costs, provided it files the 281.45 fiche for you. It comes off its profit before your pay.

data.name: Title_copyright_within_limits
data.value: Royalty within the limits

data.name: Rule_copyright_within_limits
data.value: The part of the royalty that keeps its quality of movable income: at most 30% of the royalty and your gross pay, and at most the year's cap, while your copyright income of the four previous years averaged at most that cap. It reaches your pocket taxed apart, outside your social contributions and the advance-payment surcharge.

data.name: Title_copyright_taxed_as_pay
data.value: Royalty taxed as pay

data.name: Rule_copyright_taxed_as_pay
data.value: What the royalty passes the limits by is professional income, which Netto taxes as your director pay: with your pay, in your social contributions' base, on the scale and in the advance-payment surcharge's base, though never on your payslip.

data.name: Title_copyright_tax
data.value: Tax apart on the royalty

data.name: Rule_copyright_tax
data.value: The part within the limits is taxed apart at 15%, never on the scale nor against the tax-free amount. That tax joins the State tax before the autonomy factor and the regional tax split it, so what it adds can be a cent off 15%. It is on that part less its flat-rate costs, which from 2026 only a holder of an attestation du travail des arts takes.

data.name: Title_copyright_municipal_surcharge
data.value: Municipal surcharge on the royalty

data.name: Rule_copyright_municipal_surcharge
data.value: Your municipality's rate applied to the tax the royalty adds: the surcharge is on the whole tax.

data.name: Title_copyright_low_earned_income_credit_lost
data.value: Tax credit for low earned income the royalty takes away

data.name: Rule_copyright_low_earned_income_credit_lost
data.value: The credit follows your pay alone, but your total net income, the royalty within the limits included, limits it: none above the ceiling, and from where the full credit ends up to the ceiling, at most what the same falling line gives on that total. What the royalty takes away of the credit is lost.

data.name: Title_copyright_income_tax_advance_payments
data.value: Advance-payment surcharge the lost credit adds

data.name: Rule_copyright_income_tax_advance_payments
data.value: The royalty's own tax is never surcharged. But the surcharge on your pay's tax is on that tax at 106% less what was withheld and the credit you actually get: a credit the royalty takes away raises it, less any change in the bonus.

data.name: Amount_copyright_relative_limit_rate
data.value: Share of the royalty and the pay within the limits

data.name: Amount_copyright_cap
data.value: Cap on the royalty within the limits

data.name: Amount_copyright_envelope_rate
data.value: Share of your pay and royalty an advance ruling accepts as royalty, for all of your time spent creating

data.name: Amount_copyright_taxed_apart_rate
data.value: Rate of the tax apart

data.name: Title_copyright_flat_rate_costs
data.value: Flat-rate costs on the royalty

data.name: Rule_copyright_flat_rate_costs
data.value: Without proof of real costs, the part within the limits is taxed less flat-rate costs: 50% of the first band and 25% of the next up to the second band's ceiling, nothing beyond. From 2026 they are only for works covered, when the royalty is paid, by an attestation du travail des arts of art. 7 of the law of 16.12.2022 or of art. 12 §8 of the royal decree of 13.03.2023, never one of art. 17 of that decree. They lower what is taxed apart and withheld, never what reaches your pocket, and never come off the part taxed as pay.

data.name: Title_company_contribution
data.value: INASTI's company contribution

data.name: Rule_company_contribution
data.value: The flat contribution every company pays INASTI each year, whatever it pays you: the lower amount while the balance-sheet total of its penultimate closed financial year, as it stood on 1 January, is at most the threshold, the higher one above it. A cost of the company, like its running costs, which lowers its profit: the company deducts it as a professional cost.

data.value: Contribution, balance-sheet total at most the threshold

data.name: Amount_company_contribution_upper_band
data.value: Contribution, balance-sheet total above the threshold

data.name: Amount_balance_sheet_threshold

data.name: Title_equipment_costs
data.value: Your IT and phone's costs

data.name: Rule_equipment_costs
data.value: What your IT and phone cost the company over the year, as it bears them: a cost of the company, like its running costs, which lowers its profit, deducted in full.

data.name: Title_equipment_benefit
data.value: IT and phone's benefit in kind before your contribution

data.name: Rule_equipment_benefit
data.value: Each piece's flat yearly value, per appliance: a PC 72, a tablet or a mobile phone 36, a phone subscription 48 for each phone number, the internet connection 60 once whatever their number. Provided for part of the year, each piece's value is taken for its calendar days, the first counted and the last not, rounded to the cent.

data.name: Title_equipment_contribution
data.value: Your contribution

data.name: Rule_equipment_contribution
data.value: What you pay the company for the private use of your IT and phone. It comes off the benefit you are taxed on, never more than it, and leaves your pocket for the company.

data.name: Title_equipment_benefit_taxed
data.value: IT and phone's benefit in kind after your contribution

data.name: Rule_equipment_benefit_taxed
data.value: The benefit less your contribution. It is director pay never paid in cash: in your social contributions' base, your income tax and the monthly withholding.
